title: Madeira
subtitle: Heat, oxygen and acidity
objectives: Explain estufagem and canteiro in detail
Explain Tinta Negra and the noble grapes

steps.title: Estufagem and canteiro
steps.body: Estufagem heats wine in stainless steel tanks to 45 to 50 degrees for at least three months, then rests it; this is used mainly for younger wines. Canteiro ages wine in casks in warm lofts, called armazéns, for years, sometimes decades. Canteiro is slower and gentler, giving finer, more complex wines. The best Madeiras are all canteiro.
steps.highlight: Estufagem: fast heat. Canteiro: slow warmth.

steps.title: Age categories
steps.body: Madeira labels show age: 5 years, called Reserve; 10 years, Special Reserve; 15 years, Extra Reserve; and 20, 30, 40 and 50 years. Colheita is a single vintage aged at least five years. Frasqueira, or Vintage, comes from a single noble grape and year, aged at least 20 years in cask.

steps.prompt: What is required for a Frasqueira Madeira?
options: A single noble grape, a single year and 20 years in cask
steps.explanation: Frasqueira is the top category: one grape, one vintage, 20 years minimum in cask.

steps.title: Grapes
steps.body: The noble white grapes, Sercial, Verdelho, Boal and Malvasia, define sweetness when named on the label. Terrantez is a rare fifth. Tinta Negra, a black grape, makes most Madeira; since 2015 its name can appear on labels. Madeira keeps high acidity, with sugar ranging from under 50 g/l in Sercial to over 100 g/l in Malvasia.

steps.prompt: Order these Madeira age categories from youngest to oldest.
steps.explanation: Each step requires longer ageing; Frasqueira also requires a single grape and year.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Estufagem heats quickly; canteiro ages slowly in warm lofts
Labels show age from 5 years to Frasqueira at 20 or more
Noble grapes define sweetness; Tinta Negra makes most Madeira
